name: media_rss_sweep
what: Live RSS sweep of 8 popular Indian newspapers' section feeds -- Economic Times, Hindu, Hindu Business Line, Times of India, Livemint, Moneycontrol, Business Standard (English) + Amar Ujala (Hindi) -- filtered for investment-intent language (English + Devanagari keywords), matched against real 23-country foreign stock-market rosters (same files layer 42 uses). Full article text pulled only for roster-confirmed hits. Originally a workaround for ET/Hindu/HBL blocking Anthropic's hosted crawler/search infra outright -- runs via subprocess curl from the local machine, which is never blocked (see feedback_economic_times_blocked memory) -- kept as the standard fetch method when extended to more sources for consistency. CAVEAT on the Hindi source: company-name matching only catches names Indian financial press conventionally leaves in Latin script (Apple, Tesla, Toyota); transliterated names (e.g. एप्पल for Apple) are invisible to the shared Latin-script matcher -- partial, not full, non-English coverage. Separate CAVEAT: 'strong' fragment matches on generic industry-descriptive company names (e.g. 'Semiconductor Manufacturing International Corp' vs. any article about semiconductor manufacturing in general) still slip through even after the SPAC/share-class filter -- treat every match here as a candidate for human review via its full_text field, not a confirmed lead, same as layer 44's un-reviewed MoU rows.

matches.company: Philip Morris International Inc Common Stock
matches.title: Philip Morris Q3 net revenues rise 5.5% to $11.4 billion on smoke-free, combustible growth
matches.full_text: New Delhi: Tobacco major Philip Morris International (PMI) reported a 5.5 per cent YoY rise in net revenues to $11.4 billion in Q3, driven by growth in both smoke-free and combustible products, as per a company statement. As per the release, PMI's total shipments rose 0.6 per cent during the quarter, supported by a 2.7 per cent increase in smoke-free product (SFP) shipments across all categories.This was backed by high single-digit growth in adjusted in-market sales of smoke-free products. The combustible products segment also remained resilient, particularly in markets where smoke-free products are banned or have limited availability. We delivered another excellent quarter, with growing total volumes, double-digit organic operating income growth and robust margin expansion,  said Jacek Olczak, Group CEO PMI.Revenues from smoke-free products increased 4.1 per cent, while the combustible products segment recorded 6.4 per cent growth. Smoke-free products, which are now available in 110 markets, contributed over approximately 42 per cent in the year-to-date period.On the other hand, the company's gross profit increased 6.7 per cent, supported by higher combustible product pricing and benefits from scale and product mix. Operating income rose 14.1 per cent during the quarter.Meanwhile, reported diluted EPS of USD 2.12 declined by 4.9 per cent, mainly due to the non-cash fair value adjustment for equity security investments.Adjusted diluted EPS grew by 5.4 per cent, or by 5.8 per cent excluding a one cent unfavorable currency impact to reach USD 2.36, marking  another quarterly all-time high,  the company said in the release.In the international smoke-free segment, net revenues increased 0.7 per cent, with organic growth of 3.4 per cent, driven by a 2.7 per cent rise in volumes.Adjusted in-market sales growth accelerated to 8 per cent, despite a challenging comparison for heated tobacco units (HTUs) due to differences in shipment timing, particularly in Japan. In this segment, gross profit rose 0.8 per cent, reflecting organic growth of 3.3 per cent.The company also raised its regular quarterly dividend by 8.8 per cent to USD 1.60 per share, equivalent to an annualised dividend of USD 6.40 per share. (ANI)

matches.title: Hinduja's Gulf Oil scouts acquisitions in Asia, South America ahead of global listing
matches.full_text: Mumbai: Gulf Oil Lubricants plans to return to Mexico in 2027, the market where the Gulf brand's journey began, as the Hinduja Group-owned company accelerates its international expansion, scouts acquisitions in new markets and prepares for a possible global listing in the next three to five years.The company also plans to re-enter the US market in 2027 through a master-licensing arrangement covering 11 states, with discussions under way to expand into other parts of the country, Sanjay Hinduja, non-executive chairman of Gulf Oil Lubricants India, told ET.The US was excluded when the Hinduja family acquired Gulf from Chevron Corp in 1984. The planned entry will mark the company's return to a market it had not been permitted to operate in under the original acquisition arrangement.The group also intends to list Gulf Oil International in the next three to five years, although the listing venue and timing have not been decided. We are still busy expanding, acquiring and growing,  said Hinduja, adding that the company was still a few years away from going public. Gulf Oil International remains privately held and does not disclose its revenue figures.Its Indian entity is listed and has a market capitalisation of â¹5, 113 crore. Last week, Gulf Oil Lubricants India reported a 34.48% year-on-year increase in net profit to â¹117 crore in the second quarter of FY27, from â¹87 crore in the corresponding period last year. Profitability was supported by volume growth across consumer, commercial and industrial segments. Revenue from operations rose 44% to â¹1,379 crore from â¹ 957 crore. Earnings before interest, tax, depreciation and amortisation increased 37.29% to â¹163 crore from â¹118 crore, while the EBITDA margin contracted 58 basis points to 11.8% from 12.4% a year earlier.Hinduja said the company was also scouting for acquisitions to strengthen its international presence. It has appointed banks to identify potential targets in South America and Southeast Asia, although investment commitments have not been finalised.Gulf Oil International has established facilities in Argentina and Brazil and is developing operations in markets including Chile, Paraguay and Bolivia. Its marine lubricants business has emerged as a key international growth driver, servicing more than 1,000 ports globally. Hinduja said the business was now the world's second-largest marine lubricants player.The group is also exploring acquisitions in Vietnam and other Southeast Asian markets.In India, Gulf Oil Lubricants plans to invest â¹55 crore to expand manufacturing capacity at its Silvassa and Chennai plants by 70%, as it seeks to accelerate growth and strengthen its domestic market position, Ravi Chawla, MD and CEO of Gulf Oil Lubricants India, said.

matches.title: Cyberattacks on banks, including AU Small Finance Bank, worry insurers as claim risks rise
matches.full_text: Mumbai: The spate of cyberattacks targeting financial institutions, including the one involving AU Small Finance Bank, is raising concerns about the growing vulnerability of banks and the potential scale of losses, with insurers reporting an increase in cyber incidents over the past three to four months.AU Small Finance Bank said it's investigating a potential data breach involving a third-party software-as-a-service platform hosted by Salesforce that holds information related to auto loan customers. The bank has a â¹100 crore cyber insurance cover from New India Assurance, which could help cushion the financial impact. However, the lender has not yet intimated the insurer, according to people familiar with the matter. The extent of the potential data exposure and the number of customers affected are yet to be established.Also read: PB Fintech's UAE insurance business grows 19-fold as it looks beyond motor coverThis follows cyberattacks involving Bank of Baroda and State Bank of India, pointing to growing risks across the banking sector.Insurers said they had witnessed a spate of attacks on financial institutions and manufacturing companies in recent months. Forensic investigations into several hacks are still underway, making it too early to determine the extent of the breaches and the potential claims. The spate of attacks we are witnessing is worrying because hackers are increasingly using artificial intelligence to breach even sophisticated security systems,  an insurance industry executive said.  Our concern is that the depth of penetration could be much higher, which could translate into significantly larger losses. 135434697While ransomware and business interruption remain major risks, financial institutions face potentially significant liabilities from the exposure of customer information, including know-your-customer documents and financial records. The costs could extend to forensic investigations, legal advice, customer notifications, public relations and credit monitoring for affected customers. The scale of the liability will depend on the nature of the information compromised, the number of customers affected and the findings of forensic investigations,  said an executive at a state-owned insurer.Cyber insurance policies typically cover expenses related to forensic investigations, business interruption, legal costs and certain data-related liabilities, subject to policy terms and exclusions. The adequacy of an institution's cover will depend on the scale of the breach and the liabilities arising from it.The recent raids could also put pressure on cyber insurance premiums, which have remained relatively subdued at 0.75-1.5% of the sum assured in recent years amid low claims, as the threat landscape becomes more complex.

matches.company: Commercial Vehicle Group, Inc. - Common Stock
matches.title: Tata Motors takes control of Iveco in €3.43-billion deal; focus shifts to debt, integration
matches.full_text: Tata Motors took control of Italian commercial-vehicle maker Iveco on Friday, acquiring an 89.42 per cent stake for approximately €3.43 billion (₹36,387 crore) after settling its cash tender offer. The acquisition gives India’s largest commercial-vehicle manufacturer control of a European business with annual revenue of ₹1.42 lakh crore, but shifts the focus to integrating operations, generating cash-flow benefits and repaying acquisition debt. TML CV Holdings B.V., Tata Motors’ indirect wholly owned subsidiary, acquired 238.16 million common shares at €14.40 apiece. The holding represents 89.42 per cent of Iveco’s common share capital, excluding treasury shares. Iveco has consequently become an indirect subsidiary of Tata Motors, the company said in an exchange filing. N. Chandrasekaran, Chairman of Tata Sons, has become Iveco’s non-executive chairperson and senior non-executive director, while Olof Persson continues as chief executive. Tata Motors executives P. B. Balaji and Girish Wagh have joined the board alongside independent directors Guenter Butschek and Charles Nichols. The acquisition also brings changes to Iveco’s board committees and voting structure, with all outstanding special voting shares repurchased for no consideration. “On Iveco, consolidation will begin next quarter, with immediate priority being to ensure a seamless transition,” Wagh, Tata Motors’ Managing Director and CEO, told investors at the October 23 earnings call, referring to the October–December quarter. Global scale, execution test Iveco reported calendar-year 2025 revenue of €13.43 billion, down approximately 6.9 per cent from €14.42 billion in 2024. The company employs 33,000 people across 16 industrial sites and 22 research and development centres. The acquisition brings Iveco’s trucks, buses, FPT powertrain technologies and vehicle-financing operations into Tata Motors’ commercial-vehicle business. Iveco’s defence operations, sold separately to Leonardo, are excluded from the transaction. In their September offer announcement, the companies estimated combined annual revenue of approximately €21 billion and vehicle sales exceeding 590,000 units. Europe accounted for about 46 per cent of the combined revenue base, India 32 per cent and South America 8 per cent. The industrial rationale rests on complementary product portfolios and geographical markets. Tata gains an established European and Latin American presence, alongside capabilities in engines, alternative fuels and electrification, while the companies seek to share technology investments, distribution networks and procurement benefits. However, converting that scale into shareholder returns will depend on the financial commitments outlined when the acquisition was announced. In its July 2025 investor presentation, Tata targeted annual free-cash-flow synergies of up to 0.5 per cent of combined revenue from FY28, earnings-per-share breakeven within two years and repayment of acquisition debt within four years

matches.company: Clean Energy Technologies, Inc. - Common Stock
matches.title: Two Point O Capital raises $10 million to expand clean energy platform
matches.full_text: Two Point O Capital (TW.O), an artificial intelligence (AI)-powered, full-stack clean energy deployment platform for commercial and industrial (C&I) businesses, has raised $10 million in a funding round led by Transition Venture Capital. Existing investor Omnivore and angel investors Chiranjeev Singh Saluja and Sudhir M Reddy also participated in the round. The funding will help TW.O expand into battery energy storage (BESS) and deepen its presence in solar, energy efficiency and wastewater treatment. It also plans to grow in energy and water-intensive sectors such as data centres, automotive, pharma, manufacturing and healthcare. The company works with leading original equipment manufacturers (OEMs) and engineering, procurement, and construction (EPC) firms across India. Its clients include Premier Energies, Godrej, JK Tyre, Morepen Pharma, Wipro and Phoenix Mills. C&I customers need customised capital and asset solutions to meet their clean energy and utility needs. These solutions can help lower operating costs, provide access to new markets such as the European Union, and improve operational resilience. The opportunity is estimated at $100 billion to $150 billion annually, which TW.O aims to address through its capital solutions. “India’s tremendous growth in C&I segments will continue to increase demand for energy and water, placing greater pressure on businesses to manage and optimise energy costs and resources,” said Karan Bhutani, chief executive officer and co-founder of TW.O. “The recent West Asia crisis has further underscored the importance of energy independence and resilience, making the transition to clean energy and efficient water utilisation an imperative rather than a choice,” he said. Bhutani said TW.O is uniquely positioned to deliver this by combining innovative capital, turnkey execution, and technology expertise to help customers reduce costs, improve resilience and become competitive. “This funding will accelerate our vision to become India’s first and largest multi-asset and multi-solution platform enabling adoption of clean energy by C&I customers,” he said  TW.O was founded in 2024 by Archit Mehrotra, Karan Bhutani, Manya Ranjan and Shashidhar Reddy, whose combined experience exceeds 75 years across firms including KKR, McKinsey, Shell, BP, Honeywell, ReNew, Sterlite Power and GIC. The company helps businesses adopt sustainable infrastructure through flexible financing, project ownership, transparent measurement and guaranteed results. The firm said that its assets under management have grown 1.5 times each quarter over the past three quarters. The company uses a proprietary AI and machine learning platform for solutioning, underwriting and asset monitoring. This enables predictive maintenance, risk mitigation and performance optimisation while keeping operating costs low. Yashodhara Bakliwal, vice president, investment at TVC said TW.O removes the capex barrier, accelerating the adoption of clean energy solutions.  Sh

matches.company: Clean Energy Technologies, Inc. - Common Stock
matches.title: Solex Energy eyeing US market for international debut, says chairman
matches.full_text: Eyeing a footprint in the global renewable energy market, homegrown Solex Energy plans to establish solar module and cell manufacturing capacities in the US as part of its $1.5 billion investment roadmap through 2030.In an interaction, the company's Chairman Chetan Shah said that while the US remains the largest global solar market, steep anti-dumping duties on Chinese imports leave India as the sole viable supplier of low-cost alternatives.When asked whether Solex Energy is exploring expansion in the US, he replied in the affirmative.Sharing the rationale behind the move, he said Solex Energy is targeting the US market for expansion primarily to capitalise on the massive global demand for clean energy components while positioning itself as a reliable, cost-effective alternative to Chinese suppliers."The US is a high-potential market. While many Indian corporates are already present there, a healthy number of business houses, including us, are also looking to invest there," Shah, who is also the Managing Director (MD) of Solex Energy, told PTI.In India, the company operates a 4 gigawatt (GW) module manufacturing facility in Gujarat, and aims to increase its capacity to 10 GW. It is also in the process of establishing 10 GW of cell manufacturing and 2 GW of ingot and wafer production.Shah did not share details of the US projects due to regulatory compliance, but said the investments will be part of the company's $1.5 billion investment plan up to 2030.A team has been formed to study various parameters, including required investments, locations in the US, among others, he said.On the ALMM-II framework, Shah said the industry is aligned with objectives of the government initiative and has made investments worth thousands of crore to set up module capacities in India to support the country's net zero goals.However, under the present market circumstances, the industry needs an extension of ALMM-II by at least 12 months on account of cell availability, he added.ALMM-II framework mandates sourcing of made-in-India cells from an approved list of module manufacturers (ALMM).As of October 2026, India had about 262 GW of module manufacturing capacity and only about 37 GW of cell capacity, he noted."Amid this huge gap between module and cell capacity in India, out of the installed capacities, most of them are of old MONO PERC technology and several capacities are also non-operational," Shah said, adding that the module capacities have been set up for use of the latest TOPcon technology.

matches.company: American Eagle Outfitters, Inc. Common Stock
matches.title: Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Q2 profit more than doubles to ₹53 crore
matches.full_text: Aditya Birla Fashion and Retail Ltd (ABFRL) on Saturday reported a twofold increase in consolidated net profit at â¹53.05 crore for September quarter FY27.The company had posted a net profit of â¹23.44 crore during July-September FY26, according to a regulatory filing from ABFRL.Revenue from operations rose to â¹2,265.61 crore from â¹2,037.90 crore earlier.Total expenses of ABFRL, which handles Pantaloons and Style Up, along with a host of ethnic brands, were at â¹2,224.99 crore, up 9.71 per cent in the second quarter of FY27.Total income, including other income, was up 11.48 per cent to â¹2,295.42 crore in Q2 FY27.Last year, the Aditya Birla Group demerged its Madura business into a separately listed entity, Aditya Birla Lifestyle Brands Limited (ABLBL), effective from May 1, 2025.ABLBL has its lifestyle brands business as Louis Philippe, Van Heusen, Allen Solly, Peter England, Simon Carter and youth western wear brands such as American Eagle. It also has a sportswear brand, Reebok, for which it has a long-term licensing agreement for the Indian market.ABFRL has its retail business under Pantaloons and Style Up, along with a host of ethnic brands, which it owns, such as Designer-led brands of Sabyasachi, Shantnu & Nikhil, House of Masaba and Tarun Tahiliani. It has premium ethnic wear brands, including Jaypore, Tasva & TCNS.

matches.title: IGL Q2 result: Net profit plunges 93.5% to ₹24 crore on higher gas costs
matches.full_text: Indraprastha Gas Ltd (IGL), the country's largest city gas distributor, reported a sharp 93.5 per cent decline in standalone net profit for the September quarter as a substantial increase in input gas costs eroded margins, offsetting higher sales volumes and revenue.Net profit fell to â¹24.38 crore in the second quarter of 2026-27 from â¹372.51 crore a year earlier, despite an 8 per cent increase in sales volumes and a 26 per cent jump in gross turnover.The company said its average daily gas sales crossed the 10 million standard cubic metres per day (mmscmd) mark for the first time, rising to 10.06 mmscmd in the July-September period from 9.31 mmscmd in the corresponding period last year.Gross sales turnover increased to â¹5,999.13 crore from â¹4,431.63 crore, reflecting higher sales as well as the impact of increased gas prices.CNG volumes grew 9 per cent year-on-year during the quarter, while piped natural gas (PNG) sales rose 8 per cent, indicating continued expansion in demand across the transport and household segments.However, the steep fall in profitability despite higher volumes and turnover highlights the pressure that rising procurement costs can exert on city gas distributors, particularly when increase in input prices cannot be fully passed on to consumers.IGL operates city gas distribution networks across 34 districts in 11 geographical areas spanning Delhi, Uttar Pradesh, Haryana and Rajasthan.Its infrastructure includes more than 30,000 km of pipelines and over 1,000 CNG stations, catering to more than 2.5 million CNG vehicles. It has also connected over 3.5 million households to piped natural gas.
